newsitem.title: FRANCE: French supreme court rejects Carlos "kidnap" plea.
newsitem.headline: French supreme court rejects Carlos "kidnap" plea.

text.p: France's highest court on Tuesday threw out a bid by jailed guerrilla mastermind "Carlos the Jackal" to win freedom by arguing he had been illegally kidnapped in Sudan and taken to France, judicial sources said.
The Cour de Cassation ruled there was no reason to study Carlos' claims that he was drugged, tied up and bundled onto a plane bound to France in August 1994, the sources said.

The ruling, overturning an appeal court decision to order an inquiry, ends efforts by Venezuelan-born Carlos, whose real name is Illich Ramirez Sanchez, to persuade French courts that he should be freed by arguing his arrest was illegal.
Carlos' lawyer said he would seek to take the case to the European Court of Human Rights, even though it has previously thrown out a similar kidnap lawsuit by Carlos.

France says Carlos killed 83 people in a gruesome series of attacks in the 1970s and 1980s, mostly in the Middle East and Europe. His most audacious was to kidnap 11 ministers at an OPEC conference in Vienna in 1975.
Carlos' lawyer Frederic Pariente said he was unable to confirm the Supreme Court ruling, saying he had not yet received written documents.

But he said: "It wouldn't surprise me. I intend to go to the European Court of Human Rights...to persuade them that the conditions of his arrest were not those laid down in international conventions."
In July, the European Commission of Human Rights, which vets cases for the rights court, said Carlos' complaints were "obviously groundless".

Pariente told Reuters that the Commission partly based its argument on the fact that Sudan was outside its jurisdiction. "That's a specious argument," Pariente said, arguing that France was clearly involved.
